records.title: Cycle detection in TaskQueue only checks direct-dep duplicates, not graph cycles
records.body:
## Problem
The cycle detection in `tasks.ts` (lines 200-208) uses a `seen` Set to detect duplicate entries within the immediate `deps` array. It does not detect real cycles such as A→B→A, where no single dependency list has duplicates.

## Why
`runAll` will enter an infinite loop when a real cycle exists: after completing all immediately-ready tasks, the remaining tasks keep appearing as 'pending with unsatisfied deps' and the loop never terminates.

## Fix
Implement a proper DFS topological-sort check: assign a new task a tentative ID, then DFS from each declared dependency and fail if the DFS visits a node that is an ancestor of the new node.

**File:** `packages/skills/src/tasks.ts`

---
**Severity:** medium  
**Labels:** bug

records.title: Issue #2: TaskService Implementation
records.body:
Implement all ~38 `TaskService` methods (`crates/core/src/service.rs`) against libSQL.

## Goal
Implement all ~38 `TaskService` methods against libSQL.

## Files
- **`crates/local-backend/src/tasks.rs`**: `LocalTaskService` implementing `TaskService` trait.

## Non-Obvious Semantics (from `crates/sacrum-client/src/queries/tasks.rs`)
1. **`short_id`**: First 6 hex chars of UUID. `resolve_short_id` = prefix lookup over `id`/`short_id`, error on zero or multiple matches.
2. **`find_path`**: BFS shortest path over `task_dependencies` in Rust.
3. **`add_dependency`**: Reject cycles (error if path exists from `depends_on_id` back to `task_id`).
4. **Ready queue (`list_ready`)**: Tasks with zero incomplete blockers (`completed_at IS NULL`) and not archived.
5. **Cascade delete**: `DeleteTask(cascade)` deletes children recursively.
6. **Archive = soft delete**: `archived` flag, not physical delete.
7. **Sections**: Singleton types (`goal`, `context`, `current_behavior`, `desired_behavior`) upsert; multi types ordered by `position`; `check_item` toggles `done`.
8. **`set_code_refs`/`sync_dependencies`**: Idempotent delete+insert in one transaction.
9. **Every mutation**: Writes `changes` row in same transaction + pushes to in-process broadcast.

## Key Trait Methods (~38)
- CRUD: `create_task`, `get_task`, `update_task`, `delete_task`, `task_exists`, `resolve_short_id`
- Listing: `list_tasks`, `list_tasks_without_lookups`, `list_tasks_with_lookups`, `list_ready`
- Relationships: `set_parent`, `remove_parent`, `add_dependency`, `remove_dependency`, `sync_dependencies`, `get_blockers`, `get_incomplete_blockers_with_details`, `find_path`, `get_parent`, `get_children`, `get_dependencies`, `get_dependents`
- Sections: `add_section`, `upsert_section`, `remove_sections`, `edit_section_by_ordinal`, `remove_section_by_ordinal`, `mark_checklist_item_done`, `toggle_checklist_item_done`
- Code refs: `add_code_ref`, `remove_code_refs`, `set_code_refs`, `append_ref`, `append_section_ref`
- Workflow: `assign_workflow`, `unassign_workflow`, `set_current_step`, `advance_to_step`
- Show: `get_task_show_bundle`, `get_task_title`, `get_task_titles`

## Acceptance Criteria
- All CRUD round-trips pass with tempdir DB.
- Dependency cycle rejection works.
- Ready queue excludes tasks with incomplete blockers.
- `resolve_short_id` returns error on ambiguity.
- Cascade delete removes all children.

records.title: Implement a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) Traversal Engine to Identify Circular Dependencies
records.body:
Domain: Graph Theory & Algorithmic Design

The application allows tasks to have prerequisites, meaning an intern must finish certain assignments before unlocking others. Currently, the system lacks checks to prevent circular dependencies, meaning a user could accidentally lock a workflow by making Task A depend on Task B, while Task B depends on Task A. Build an automated graph validation utility within the task configuration router using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) design model. Implement a cycle detection algorithm using Depth-First Search (DFS) or Topological Sorting to analyze task relationships. This engine should automatically block any updates that create a loop, giving students practical experience applying graph theory algorithms to real-world software workflows.

records.title: [Feature] Advanced Recursion Analysis (Master Theorem & Graph Traversal Patterns)
records.body:
## Summary

As noted in our [Known Limitations](https://github.com/rayhuang2006/asymptote#known-limitations), complex recursive trees and divide-and-conquer algorithms are not fully resolvable by the current analyzer. This umbrella issue tracks incremental improvements to recursion handling.

## Scope

This is a long-term effort. The following milestones break it into achievable stages:

### Phase 1: Common Recursive Patterns (regex/AST fingerprinting)
- [ ] Detect **binary search** pattern: single recursive call with `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` → O(log N)
- [ ] Detect **merge sort** pattern: two recursive calls each on `n/2` + linear merge → O(N log N)
- [ ] Detect **DFS/BFS on adjacency list**: loop over `adj[node]` with visited check → O(V + E)

### Phase 2: Basic Master Theorem Heuristics
- [ ] Identify recurrence form `T(n) = a * T(n/b) + O(n^d)` from AST
- [ ] Apply Master Theorem cases to estimate complexity
- [ ] Mark result with `(?)` confidence when detection is uncertain

### Phase 3: Backtracking & Exponential Detection
- [ ] Detect multiple recursive calls without problem-size reduction → flag as O(2^N) or O(N!)
- [ ] Detect pruning (`if` guards before recursive calls) and note it in confidence

## Non-Goals

- Formal proof-level analysis (this remains a heuristic tool)
- Handling of memoized recursion / dynamic programming (separate issue)

## Why This Matters

Recursion is central to competitive programming. Even rough estimations (e.g., "this looks exponential") are valuable for catching TLE-prone submissions before testing.

records.title: Planner cleanup: adopt Kahn's topological sort, prune the acyclic search, factor propagate() duplication
records.body:
Review pass over `adam-rs`'s planner (`planner.rs`, `matching.rs`, `release.rs`, `digraph.rs`, `scc.rs`, `seed.rs`) and `sheet.rs`'s `propagate`/`execute_plan`. Out of scope for PR #185 (seedfill); tracked here for later. Ranked by value.

## High value

### 1. Replace the hand-rolled Tarjan SCC (`planner/scc.rs`) with Kahn's topological sort, deleting the module

`tarjan_scc` (~180 lines) has exactly two callers, and both want something simpler than full SCC:

- `plan()` runs `tarjan_scc`, reverses it, asserts every component is size 1, and flattens — i.e. it wants *a topological order, or a cycle error*. Kahn's gives both directly: the emitted order is the execution order; any nodes left un-emitted are a `FilterCycle`.
- `is_acyclic()` computes `tarjan_scc(...).all(len == 1)` — it wants *a boolean*, but allocates a `Vec<Vec<Node>>` of components just to check their sizes.

Adopting Kahn's for both removes the whole `scc.rs` module and makes `plan()`'s intent obvious. Net-negative lines. Needs test validation that the (still valid) topological order among independent steps doesn't shift any observable behavior.

### 2. `is_acyclic` is the hot loop and does the most wasteful work

`search_acyclic` (the `M^R` exhaustive search behind `Assignment::solve_acyclic`) calls `is_acyclic` at *every complete leaf*, and `is_acyclic` rebuilds the digraph and runs full Tarjan each time. Two independent wins:

- **Per-leaf:** a DFS 3-color cycle check (or Kahn's, per #1) avoids the component-vector allocation.
- **Structural:** `search_acyclic` only checks acyclicity at complete leaves. It could prune mid-tree — reject a partial assignment the moment it forms a cycle — turning the `M^R` brute force into branch-and-bound. Bigger change, but it directly attacks the planner's one exponential.

## Medium

### 3. `resolve` re-runs the full exponential `solve_acyclic` C+1 times from scratch

The greedy release loop in `release.rs` re-solves the entire matching + acyclicity search once per cell-release candidate. The known incremental alternative — maintain the matching and *augment* when a cell is forbidden (SkyBlue/DeltaBlue incremental style) — is noted as "Future Work" in the 2026-08-04 cyclic-planner design doc. This is the real scaling ceiling.

### 4. Factor the `plan -> build_seeds -> execute_plan` triple in `propagate()`

`sheet.rs` `propagate()` does the identical three-step in both Phase 1 (pre-plan for conditional match cells) and Phase 3 (general plan). A small `plan_and_execute(active, &mut violations)` helper removes the duplication and the two easy-to-desync `build_seeds` call sites.

### 5. `resolve`'s per-cell `released.clone()`

Each greedy step clones the whole released set to add one cell. `released.insert(cell)` / `released.remove(cell)` on failure avoids the allocation. Minor, but it's in the C-iteration loop.

## Low / framing

### 6. Name the algorithms in the docs

`Assignment::solve` / `try_assign` is Kuhn's bipartite matching by augmenting paths (with an undo trail); saying so orients a reader faster than re-deriving it. `resolve` is greedy-by-weight over a downward-closed (gammoid) independence system — the design doc says this, the code comment doesn't.

### 7. `forced_output_cells` overlaps with the matching's own infeasibility detection

It's a separate fixpoint computing "cells that can never be a source," purely informational (UI). Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition of the matching yields exactly that set (the always-matched vertices) as a byproduct, so if the matching ever moves to a DM-based structure this fixpoint could fold in. Research-y; not worth doing standalone.

## Suggested first step

**#1 + #2 together** — one coherent change (standardize on Kahn's / a DFS cycle check, delete `scc.rs`), net-negative lines, hitting the one hot path.

records.title: Stack overflow during semantic verification of multi-hop transfers
records.body:
The compiler stack overflows during semantic verification when evaluating implicit multi-hop memory transfers via Dijkstra's algorithm.

**Cause:**
`src/sema/expr.rs` automatically rewrites transfers like `transfer(tensor, RemoteHbm)` into an explicit path e.g. `transfer(transfer(tensor, NicRam), RemoteHbm)`.
However, because both `NicRam` and `RemoteHbm` dynamically fall back to the same parent `Topology::NPU(0)` inside the `Type::Pinned` representation, the compiler loses the exact intermediate `MemorySpace`. 
When it re-evaluates the inner transfer's type, it extracts `MemorySpace::NPUHBM` instead of `MemorySpace::NicRam`. This triggers another multi-hop rewrite, leading to infinite recursion and a stack overflow.

**Fix:**
Extract the exact memory space directly from `TransferExpr.space` instead of the type's default memory space when re-evaluating explicit intermediate transfers.
